plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous flowering tree that produces masses of delicate, slightly fragrant blossoms before its leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted cherry tree in Japan and in cherry blossom displays around the world.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Cherry blossom festivals (hanami) in Japan have been celebrated for over a thousand years, and forecasters track the 'cherry blossom front' as it moves north across the country.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler outer petals. It carpets woodlands and meadows in early spring and is the ancestor of many garden daffodils.
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids such as lycorine, which is why deer and rodents avoid them. Galantamine, a compound from related Narcissus species, is used in medicine for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of pea-like flowers burst directly from bare branches and even the trunk. Heart-shaped leaves follow after flowering.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, northern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mildly tart flavor. The tree shows cauliflory, meaning flowers grow directly from old wood on the trunk and larger branches.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree that is famous for its spectacular canopy of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers, which also carpet the ground beneath. Fernlike foliage gives it a feathery look.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (March to May); October to December in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, India, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
